situation: You live in a high-rise building, and you received a complaint letter from your neighbor.

body: I am sorry to inform you that your disturbance made some inconveniences for me and my family last night. You should consider other neighbors when you hold any gatherings in your flat. I hope that you will not cause loud noise anymore. I really appreciate your future actions to prevent such noise.

task11: Write a letter to your friend, who is also your neighbor. Write about your feelings about this complaint letter and what plans you have to prevent such inconveniences. Write about 50 words.
task12: Write a letter to your neighbor. Write about your feelings about this complaint letter and what plans you have to prevent such inconveniences. Write about 120-150 words.

part2.context: You are participating in an online discussion for language learners.
part2.question: Should students not be allowed to use smartphones at schools?
part2.instruction: Post your response, giving reasons and examples. Write 180-200 words.

samples.t11:
Dear Jack,
I just received a complaint letter from Mr. Edward about the noise during our gathering last night. I feel quite upset because we only wanted to have a good time. To prevent this in the future, I plan to keep the volume down and inform neighbors in advance about any gatherings. Let's discuss this when we catch up!
Best,
Alex
samples.t12:
Dear Mr. Edward,

Thank you for your letter regarding the noise from our gathering last night. I sincerely apologize for any inconvenience it caused you and your family. It was not my intention to disturb anyone, and I appreciate you bringing this to my attention.

To ensure that this will not happen again, I plan to keep future gatherings smaller and more low-key. I will also make sure to inform my neighbors in advance, so they are aware of any events. Additionally, I will be more mindful of the noise levels, especially during late hours.

I value the harmony of our community and want to maintain a good relationship with all my neighbors. Thank you for your understanding, and I hope to avoid any further disturbances in the future.

Warm regards,
Alex
samples.p2:
The question of whether students should be allowed to use smartphones at school is a really hot topic with strong arguments on both sides. Personally, I lean towards allowing them, but with clear guidelines and educational integration.

On one hand, smartphones are undeniable distractions. When a student's phone is buzzing with notifications during a lesson, it's incredibly hard for them to focus on the teacher or the material. This can lead to decreased learning and poorer academic performance. We've all seen examples of students scrolling through social media or playing games instead of paying attention. This constant temptation can really hinder the educational environment.

However, smartphones are also incredibly powerful tools that can actually enhance learning. Many educational apps, online research tools, and even digital textbooks are accessible via smartphones. For instance, a student could use their phone to quickly look up an unfamiliar word, access a relevant historical document for a project, or even use a language learning app during breaks. Banning them entirely removes these educational opportunities.

Therefore, instead of an outright ban, I believe schools should focus on teaching responsible digital citizenship and integrating smartphones as learning aids. Setting clear rules, like phones being put away during direct instruction but allowed for specific research tasks, could be a good compromise.
